```python
import re
from lxml import etree

def extract(data: bytes) -> dict:
    # Parse the XML data
    root = etree.fromstring(data)
    
    # Extract title
    title = root.find('.//h1').text.strip()
    
    # Extract blocks
    blocks = []
    for child in root.findall('.//div[@class="left_zw"]'):
        block = {}
        block['kind'] = child.find('.//p[@class="text"]/text()').strip()
        block['text'] = child.find('.//p[@class="text"]/text()').strip()
        block['xpath'] = child.get('xpath', '')
        blocks.append(block)
    
    # Extract metadata
    metadata = {}
    for child in root.findall('.//div[@class="adEditor"]'):
        metadata[child.find('.//span[@class="right"]').text.strip()] = child.find('.//span[@class="right"]').get('href', '')
    
    # Extract excluded
    excluded = {}
    for child in root.findall('.//div[@class="adEditor"]'):
        excluded[child.find('.//span[@class="right"]').text.strip()] = child.find('.//span[@class="right"]').get('href', '')
    
    # Extract warnings
    warnings = {}
    for child in root.findall('.//div[@class="adEditor"]'):
        warnings[child.find('.//span[@class="right"]').text.strip()] = child.find('.//span[@class="right"]').get('href', '')
    
    return {
        'title': title,
        'blocks': blocks,
        'metadata': metadata,
        'excluded': excluded,
        'warnings': warnings
    }
```

This function parses the XML data, extracts the required information, and returns it in a structured dictionary.
